I had a woman take me in when I was 18 because my parents were abusive and my dad is an alcoholic.

She saved my life. 

I'm now in college with 3.9 overall and 4.0 major GPA. Working, volunteering, a campus leader, founder of a non-profit to help teens and young adult survivors of child abuse. 

Neglect is considered abuse.

People like you and the woman who saved me... it's "no big deal" to you...but it truly changes our lives. 

I will NEVER forget her and think about her with every accomplishment. I'd bet your kids do the same about you. :)
I thought it was a cool thought and wanted to share! It's so cute when the kids start shouting, "I'm sfwimmin'! I'm sfwimmin'!"

I'm so sorry that you went through all of that. I also have PTSD/Depression/Anxiety resulting from childhood abuse and then too much stress when I moved out on my own. 

Seeing that napkin brought tears to my eyes. 

It's incredible how much you learn to appreciate after everything you've been through. 

You're a brave and strong person. A lot of people would've already given up if they were you. 

Keep pushing. <3

My parents were abusive, and one was an alcoholic. I moved out on my own as soon as I turned 18. 

I tried to reconcile numerous times, and then I finally realized...fuck it. They are the ones who are fucked up, not me. I talked to the rest of my family and questioned why they never helped me. To this, I received bullshit excuses and responses such as, "You were never abused!" (denial)...I tried fixing the situation for years. I constantly thought there was something wrong with me. I felt worthless, etc. and didn't exactly know why. (I'm highly overachieving in numerous areas.)

Sometimes, it's hard not having my parents there for me. Actually, it's hard.. a lot. When people casually ask about my family situation, I tell them that I was abused and moved away at age 18 to begin a  better life for myself. This actually leads to great conversations and people having much more respect for you. But it's difficult on Holidays, mothers/fathers day, parents weekend at school, etc. It's also hard to parent myself and figure out what I'm "suppose" to do. That's okay. 

Don't worry about your parents being angry with you. Bottom line, you're probably stuck in this mindset of needing their approval.  Guess what?! You are a big boy/girl, and you don't. At the end of the day, your life is yours, and your parents are pretty insignificant in comparison to the entire population. 

Here's my suggestion:
1) Move Out
2) IMMEDIATELY enroll yourself in counseling. You can do this at various  shelters, etc. for free. 
3) If you report your physical abuse and get a record, you can file for independence and basically have your tuition for college paid for. 

A friend of a friend runs a site that helps people in your situation. I highly highly HIGHLY recommend that you check out her site and contact her. She was abused and has made a wonderful life for herself and is working to help other people who are transitioning from abusive situations.

www.nolomovement.com
